utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. And good morning to those in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Good morning, Your Honours. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see the new witness is ready. Good morning to you, sir. Would you please read aloud the affirmation that is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Please sit down. Now, there are some questions for you this morning. Mr. Behar will ask the first questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Thank you very much for joining us here today. I'm going to begin, if we can, by asking you to look at a document --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: -- that contains some personal information related to you. This is 65 ter number 02513, and it's at tab 2513 there at the witness binder you have. I think it's just been handed to you. Can you just read that quietly to yourself, sir, and can you tell me now is the information on that document, your name, date, and place of birth correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that pseudonym sheet under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01093 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just a reminder, sir, before we move on that I'll be referring to you as K74 here today in order to protect your identity and that will be true for all the parties here today. I understand, sir, that on the 23rd of April, 1999, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor about the events that you experienced in Kosovo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And have you had the opportunity to read that statement before coming to court today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that there are several things that you'd like to clarify about that statement. I'll take you through those clarifications one by one, and I can just say up front, sir, one of the things that I'm hoping to do today to assist the Trial Chamber is to focus on distinguishing the things that you saw personally and some of the things that you learned from other people. I'm going to be referring here to 65 ter 2517.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And perhaps it would be helpful if the witness could be provided with a copy of that statement as well. It's in the binder under that tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, we'll begin at page 3, it's page 3, paragraph 4, in the English. There's a line that states -- I can just read it out loud to you. A line states: "At this house, the daughter, Shpresa Cana, aged 43, opened the door and was shot dead immediately ..." My first question for you, sir, is: Are those events -- is that event something that you saw personally or is that something that you were told about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it myself. Others told me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And today are you still confident to say that Shpresa Cana "opened the door and was shot dead immediately ..."?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I cannot certify it because, as I said, I didn't eye-witness it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The next reference I'll make, in the English this is at page 3, the final paragraph, I believe it's the same in the B/C/S. The fourth line states and I'll read it aloud again. "They machine-gunned every room of my houses and ensured that the burning was complete ..." And again then my question for you, sir -- my first question: Was that something you saw personally or were you told about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it personally, but after the offensive was over when we went in the direction of Albania we saw the holes of the bullets and that was all. We didn't see more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see. So is that a conclusion then that you reached based on that evidence you described seeing when you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. My next reference is from page 4, paragraph 4, of the statement --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I also have some photos. We took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Photos of the aftermath, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, the photographs of the aftermath, when we came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question refers to a statement which states -- a line that states: "The Serb attackers then went on the other side of the street to the compound of Luli Vejsa ..." And I understand there was something that you wanted to clarify with respect to the timing of that event or the timing as it sounds from that statement. Is that something that you can address?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And in the place in which it's inserted when it says: "The Serb attackers then went on the other side of the street to the compound of Luli Vejsa ..." Are you confident about the sequence in which Luli Vejsa's house was burned, or are you unsure about the timing of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I am uncertain about the time, but everything that I say has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that. Just to put that back to you, sir, just so we're clear. You're saying you are confident about the burning. You're just not sure when in the order of houses were burned that it was burned; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that same paragraph there's another sentence that says: "Luli's house was not connected to any other houses, therefore it was a target for the Serbs." Is there something you wanted to clarify about that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I don't think there is anything I want to clarify because he had a neighbour who was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Was Luli's house connected to a Serb house or did it stand -- was it independent?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It was separate -- independent. It was far from it, about 1 or 2 metres. It was separated by a narrow street.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see, sir. I think I understand that position now. And just so I'm clear then, was it still a target, as you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was a target in the sense that they were bad persons and they wanted -- the Serbs wanted to shoot at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I think we have your -- I think we have your position on that. I'll take you to page 5, the second paragraph, there's a line there that states: "I saw Luli's house bursting in flames." Is that accurate that you saw the house bursting in flames?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And is that something you were made aware of in another manner, that Luli's house had burned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: At the time we saw it after we left, the whole neighbourhood was burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And so if I'm understanding it right is that you saw the house burning but you didn't see when it first burst into flames, when it first started burning; am I understanding that correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for clarifying that. At page 6, paragraph 2 - it's actually in paragraph 1 of the B/C/S for my friend - there is a sentence that states: "When I got near my house, I saw a man standing outside my front gate with a rifle so I did not risk my life for the car." Now, I understand, sir, you may be able to clarify where it was exactly that you saw the man standing.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The man was standing in a part which belonged to the Serbs, in -- out in the street, across the -- across my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So he wasn't standing directly outside your front gate but he was standing across from the house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: He was about 100 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. With those clarifications or changes having been made, I'd like to ask you: Other than the changes that you already made when you testified in the Milutinovic case, are you satisfied that the changes -- pardon me, are you satisfied that the information contained in your statement now is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that witness statement. The unredacted version is 2517 and that's to be tendered under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01094, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: There is also a redacted version of that same statement to be tendered as a public exhibit, that's 65 ter 02532. I would seek to tender that as well, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01095.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall testifying at the trial of Milan Milutinovic on the 29th of November, 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are again dealing with correcting the transcript. My position is that this is no way to correct the transcript. He should be asking the witness, and then on the basis of the answer correct the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We had occasion to mention that again yesterday, Mr. Djurdjic. The procedure is one we are satisfied with. Please carry on, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that there's one thing, one issue, you wanted to clarify that's presently recorded in the transcript. I'll read this section out loud to you, and for my friend and the Chamber I can indicate it's at page 7513 of the transcript at line 15. And at that point, sir, an exchange takes place. There is a question: "Q. Apart from the corrections you've made, you've gone through your statement, are there any other corrections you want to make?" There was an answer there: "A. Yes, when it says Mentor Deda was hanged, I didn't say this. I said that he was killed in the yard." Is there something you wanted to clarify about that passage?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Mentor Deda is still alive. Yes, Mentor Deda is still alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And who was it that you were meaning to refer to there in that passage that was being corrected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I meant his nephew.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is that Argjend Demjaha?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Just again at line 22 is a similar change. The question was: "Q. But did you see him when he was killed or you heard it from other people?" And your answer was: "A. No, Mentor Deda -- I heard that mentor Deda is dead." Again, is there a clarification or something you wanted to explain about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I meant Argjend.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Having said that, does this -- sorry, were you saying something there --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It was Mentor who said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. In other words, when you heard -- you heard that Argjend was dead, it was Mentor who told you; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes. Mentor was the one who passed through -- who jumped through the wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, having made that clarification or those comments, does the transcript now accurately reflect your evidence and would you testify to those same facts today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would seek to tender that transcript, 65 ter number 05063.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01096.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I can now provide a very brief summary of this witness's evidence. K74 was a resident of Djakovica. He describes Serb police and paramilitaries burning down Albanian houses and killing Albanian civilians in the town in April of 1999. He testifies about the houses that were burnt down and the people who lived in those houses. He also testifies about the killing of civilians. K74 also describes how he and about 500 other people hid in an elevated neighbourhood of the village and eventually moved in a convoy towards the Albanian border. He describes police directing them along the way, and he describes that he recognised one of the officers. At the border, police took and confiscated their identification documents. That is the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I do have some questions for you in the limited time that we have remaining. As I mentioned before, one of the things that I'm hoping to do here was to distinguish some of the things that you saw personally from things that you learned or that you heard from other people. And my first question, this relates again for my friend, for the Chamber, to page 2 of your statement, the second paragraph, you describe that Serb paramilitaries had set up their operations at Stella Construction Material, which I take it is a building, and you described that they had snipers and that that caused you to live in fear? My question relating to that is: Did you see those snipers yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We saw them entering and leaving the place because they used to go in and go out often.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you yourself see something that caused you to conclude that there were snipers there and can you describe what that was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I saw them going in and out, other than going there for a purpose, one wouldn't go there. They went there to look round, to see what was going on around that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And was there an -- did you see the guns or did you see guns that made you think that they were snipers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't see weapons or guns, but that was the general belief, that people were there for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Just before we move on, can you just explain then when it was that you were making these observations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Before NATO strikes began.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And I think you may have mentioned a month before. I'm not sure if -- I think I heard that earlier. Can you give us an approximation of the amount of time before the NATO strikes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: About two or three weeks before NATO air-strikes began. I can't recall exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, there's a paragraph in your statement that appears to contain a number of different ideas and passages that seems to have caused some confusion in your previous testimony, and I'd like to see if you can help us to break it down and to understand what it was that you saw or didn't see and when that took place. The reference for my friends, this is at page 4, paragraph 6 of the statement. I'll just read you the parts I'm interested about, sir. The first part of that sentence states: "Since the very first night of NATO bombing, they were patrolling the streets, holding hand-held lamps, and sending signals to each other." Can you tell us, sir, is that what -- what you described in that line, is that something you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: This was prior to the strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us when that would have been then, the dates roughly that you saw that, the time-period that you saw that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: A long time has passed since then, but I would say about 10 or 15 days before the bombing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And again, just so we're clear, is it -- is that something that you saw? Did you see the people patrolling the streets, sending signals to each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I already said this, two or three weeks before that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. What I'm just trying to understand, sir, just so we're absolutely clear, I'm trying to distinguish -- or just to make sure that we know that that's something that you saw as opposed to something that you were told by somebody else. I'm just wondering if you can clarify for the Judges. Is -- did you see that yourself, what you've described here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it myself. They were using hand-held lamps and they -- these persons belonged to the two Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you tell us what those people were wearing, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I didn't see the persons. I saw the lights, the lamps they were holding at night. It was dark then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain what you saw to us just so that the Trial Chamber has an understanding of what this would have looked like to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I saw the lamps, hand-held lamps, from a distance of 50 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you described them sending signals to each other. Can you explain how they were sending those signals? I know it may be a basic question, but if you can just explain what it looked like.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: How shall I explain that? Short signals with the light of the torches.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you were just making a gesture there, sir, I can note for the record that appeared to be moving your thumb up and down. Am I understanding that correctly? Is that showing turning -- turning the lights on and off? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. We call it hand-held lamps. It's a torch.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. The next line of that statement is talking about burnings, and it states: "Some of the men who did the burnings had painted faces, blackened ..." It goes on to say: "The men that I saw do this burning" are "... men that I know and recognise." Following that there is a long list of men who are identified and described Pitulic Novak, Milos Scepanovic, et cetera. Just so that we're clear, I know you testified in the Milutinovic case that despite what it says in the statement you yourself didn't personally see those men do the burning and killing; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You have said that you believed those men were responsible. Are you able to tell us why you say that, why you reached that conclusion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: That day when we left for Albania, they gathered there in the neighbourhood. They were sort of analysing everything, all of us were, and from then we didn't see them anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Am I understanding right, sir, that it's a conclusion that you reached based on what you'd seen, the behaviour you'd seen prior to the actual burnings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, after it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sorry, after what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: After the burning and the killings took place, all the people of the neighbourhood gathered as we set off for Albania and we analysed the situation and we reached the conclusion that only them could have done that, as only the Serb houses were left intact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see, sir. So I think that's clear then. So it's a conclusion you reach afterwards, speaking with other villagers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. You also described in your statement what I would characterise as observations of the aftermath of what had -- what you saw after the burnings had taken place. You say, this is at the bottom of page 5: "Later at about 6.30 a.m. I and a few other men went into our neighbourhood to examine the destruction. I saw that all our houses, the properties described above, destroyed and burnt to the ground -- were destroyed and burnt to the ground." Are you able to describe to the Trial Chamber what you actually -- what you saw, how it looked when you came out and observed your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We saw a total destruction of houses and of the walls around the houses. Everything had been burnt to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you give us an idea of the scale or the size of the destruction of -- the number of houses or how much of the neighbourhood had been affected?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In the neighbourhood it was the row of the houses where my house is, about 10 to 12 houses all together only in the row where my house is. That would be the approximate number, 12 to 13 houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Moving to a bit of a different area, at page 6 and paragraph 3 of your statement, you describe gathering with your family and about 500 people in total in an elevated neighbourhood. You describe moving from there through the city towards the border. And you described police separating people at that point, separating people with vehicles from pedestrians. Is that something you observed, the police doing that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It was a huge number of people, about 1.500 from my neighbourhood. We were directed to go on foot, and the others who were in vehicles were directed in another direction. So it was not only me who saw that. Everybody saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand. And just so we're very clear, what you're describing here, these are things that you personally saw; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you. And I know you described police directing people towards Prizren and the border at Morina, and you described them directing pedestrians, including you and your family towards Qafe Prush. One of the things you explain in your statement is that one of the police directing the civilians was the person named Zika. Can you explain to us how you knew Zika?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I used to know him because he lived in my neighbourhood 500 metres away from my house. The neighbourhood where I lived was -- had many Serbs living there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And how did you know that he was a police officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Well, Gjakova is a small town.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So, is this something you knew from seeing him or from speaking to people; are you able to explain that to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: This is something I knew myself. I've seen him dressed as a policeman, and as I said he lived in my neighbourhood 500 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. You described going to the border. Can you tell us how it was that you got there? Did you walk the whole way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We followed the following route Brkoc-Vokov-Zup on foot. We had some disabled people with us in wheelchairs from our neighbourhood. So we helped them move along with us. So all of us walked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Can you explain how long it took? Do you know how long it took you to get from there to the border from the time you left until the time you arrived at the border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I wouldn't know exactly how long it took us to get there, but I would estimate about five or six hours, maximum seven.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you describe what the conditions were like as all of you walked to the border?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We all had to walk, elder, children, disabled persons. You can imagine what the conditions were. They were disastrous.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you give us a sense of the number of people who were walking this same route with you along the way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: When we reached the centre of the town there were about 1.000 or 2.000 people then. When we continued towards the border -- and at the border itself the number of people grew. I would say we were about 7.000 or 8.000 all together.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you described that at the border the police asked everyone for documents. This is at page 6, paragraph 3. You described that you handed over your identity card, that you hid your passport. Did you see what they did with your identity card when you gave it to them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. We only threw them in a box that was there, and crossed the border. We didn't have any problems at that stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So you're describing throwing them in a box. Is that something they asked you to do? Did you throw them? Did they throw them? Did they ask you to do that? Can you explain that for us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There were two of them in uniform. I didn't recognise them. I didn't know them. They only instructed us to throw the documents in the box and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you -- did you get a sense or were you able to see how many other ID cards were in there, just in terms of a large number, small number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Not a very large number when I crossed into Albania -- because I was amongst the first ones that crossed into Albania that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And were they asking everyone to do that, sir, put their identities in there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: We were a large crowd when we were told to throw away the documents into this box. They didn't search us, body search us, they just told us to throw the documents into this box and that's what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you very much for your patience. Those are my questions for you, and my learned friend from the Defence will have some questions for you now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Behar. It is now time for questions by Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I'm a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. With me is Madam Marie O'Leary, another member of my team. I have several questions for you to clarify certain points concerning your statements that you've given so far. I hope I won't be repeating some of the questions that have been put to you already. I would like just to go deeper into matters and to clarify certain things. Witness, what I'm interested in is in March 1999, with whom did you live?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: With my family. Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which members of the family you lived with in March 1999 and at the time of the events that you are testifying about here.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: With my immediate family.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who were the members of your family in 1999 who were with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: My wife, my children, my mother, my sister, my brother-in-law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And of those members of your immediate family, who was absent at the time, in March 1999, and lived with you otherwise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, I think we may need to redact that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Carry on, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, should we go into private or closed session or should we redact this afterwards? I don't know which method you are going to use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in the process of redaction now. I thought you had been spoken once and you wouldn't be repeating it. We can redact twice, but if you're going to ask many more questions like that, we would be better in private session. But I think we can carry on as we are. The next point to bear in mind, Mr. Djurdjic, is there is quite a delay between you speaking and the witness hearing the interpretation in Pristina. So you will have to wait with patience to get a reply. Would you like now to get an answer to your question? You were asked, sir, whether you lived at a house number in 1999, in March. Do you remember the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The number is important, is it, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the witness does not remember. Let's go forward. I wanted to ask him some -- about layout, certain questions, but let's go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He didn't remember your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you give your house number when you gave your statement on the 23rd of April in Tirana?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I did give the house number.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please see Exhibit P823, page 35, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note that the witness said: The number of his house has changed since then but due to overlapping the answer didn't enter into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, what I'm going to ask you refers to 1999. If I'm going to change the period I'm going to indicate. I know that your name has been probably renamed. Witness, this is a map of Djakovica furnished by the Prosecution. Could you please draw us ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I'm sorry for the interruption. Would it be possible for counsel to give the ERN number because our page 35 is not a map of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, K036-6676. That is supposed to be a map of Djakovica. And this is a map of Leposavic. Page 35 -- just a second, Madam O'Leary is going to inform me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, I believe the ERN reference was sufficient. I believe we have it. It's hard copy page number 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. You're correct. That is the map I'm after. Could we zoom in, please. What does the witness see, the hard copy, or what we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, anyway, Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you please draw on this map the neighbourhood that your street was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or maybe we should zoom out because we won't be able to see what the witness is drawing since he has a hard copy. Let's deal with the hard copy here as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could the witness please draw a circle around the neighbourhood in which he was living.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't find out where it was because I see that here there is the entire neighbourhood. I see all the other neighbourhoods but not my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But, Witness, can we then approach it in a different way and then we might get there more easily. Can you tell me where the old centre of Djakovica was situated, where is the old town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The old centre is in the centre of the town on the road that takes you to Brkoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, let me try to help you because I'm not that familiar with Djakovica, but under number 32, if you have a look you'll see that it says that that's the bus station. So can you orient yourself if you can find number 32 and where it says the bus station under this number, 32.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It says the neighbourhood of Qyli. I don't see the bus stop written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On the map, on the right side, you can see the key with all numbers and number 32 says bus station, it should be the bus station, and I thought of this that it might help you orient yourself. Can you see the number 32? You can see Lagjja e Qylit, if you can see the Qylit mosque, under the mosque there is the number 32. Or if that is easier, under number 1 we have the UNMIK building. I think that this was after June 1999. That's under number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can lower it a bit, please, so that we can see number 1. More please. There. Now it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If you can see the mosque, that's the Sefes mosque, can you see where it is, left from it is number 1. That's where the UNMIK building should be located. Can you recognise this part of Djakovica now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I know where the mosque is in the Sefes neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And can you see here number 3 written in Roman numerals, then to the left of it is number 1 and then we see the red road, that's the main road leading through Djakovica, and if it leads from Prizren towards Decani and Pec. Can you see this red road? That's the main road leading through Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see where the Pastrik Hotel is? Can you tell us that? Or any other spot that you can use to orient yourself, either the Pastrik Hotel or the place where the other mosque is or where the old barracks in Djakovica are, or if you can tell me where this village or settlement that is on an elevated spot is located or any other landmark that you might find so that you could tell us about the other locations afterwards.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I know where Hotel Pashtrik is, it is situated in the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well -- and could you please mark the centre of the Djakovica town on this map so that I could see where the centre is. You should be able to recognise it and to say this is where the centre of the town is, and then we'll see where other neighbourhoods are. Let me help you. On the right side you'll see that it says Orahovac is located 17 kilometres away --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The witness is already drawing. I don't think you need to help him mark the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours -- but we don't know what the witness is drawing. We cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exactly. The Court Officer --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, sorry for the interruption. If I could intervene for one moment. First of all, I think counsel should be advised that the hard copy we have here in Pristina is a black-and-white copy. Counsel had referred to the red road going through the centre. Since we have a black-and-white copy, obviously we're not going to see the colour. The second thing is the witness hasn't made any markings yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to thank the usher. I also have a black-and-white copy. I got on my screen a copy in colour. So the road is black, but then on the right side you will see where it says Orahovac 17 kilometres away. And in the upper left-hand corner it says Decani 17 and a half kilometres. So this should be a landmark for the main road, if you can see it. On the right-hand side it says "Orahovac" and then in the upper part on the left "Decani."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you find your way around?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the answer is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you want me to find?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You said earlier you know where the Hotel Pastrik is. Are you able to see on the map the position of that hotel, the Hotel Pastrik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't -- when I said I know where it is; I didn't mean where it is in the map because, to tell you the truth, I can't find my way around in this map. I don't understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, that is the impression we are forming here, that the witness is not a person who reads maps. Many people are like that, of course. So you may have to adjust your cross-examination in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Let me try to do this verbally.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the road leading from Orahovac towards Decani is the main road that leads through Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: From Rahovec it goes to Decan you mean? You come from Rahovec, you enter Gjakove, and then you go towards Decan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And now please tell me, from this road, where in relation to that road is the neighbourhood where you lived situated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It is in quite an opposite direction where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell us which is this opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps I could help. If you were coming from Rahovec and going towards Decani, on that road, where you lived, is that on the right side or on the left side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are asking me about where I lived?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you come from Rahovec, it is on the right-hand side. This is how I can explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you go through the centre of the town before you turn to the right to your house or is your house on the right before you reach the centre of the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the same both ways, either if you come from the road or the other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us how far from that road is your house, is it half a kilometre? One kilometre? Or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One kilometre and a half or two. I'm not accurate but around about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And as we can see on this map there is also a third road, that's the road leading to Klina. So would you pass by this junction, the crossroads, where you can go in the direction of Klina before you reach your neighbourhood or was your neighbourhood located before you reach that junction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, it is at the crossroads where the roads divide, separate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, in the centre of the town there is a place where the road for Klina leads to the right and straight, the road leading to Decani, continues. So there's this forking in the centre of the town. I'm asking you whether your neighbourhood was ahead of this crossroads, before you reach it, or after you pass it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: After you cross the -- pass this crossroad.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And please tell me what important building is located at the crossroads of the main road and the road that you would take to move in the direction of Klina, to the right, what are the buildings located there? Because I can see that this is the very centre of Djakovica town.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Hotel Pashtrik used to be there on the right side and the palace of culture. Then you continue straight to Kline.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me, this place where the palace of culture and the Pastrik Hotel are situated, is that the centre of the old Djakovica town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: That is the only centre we have. You may call it old or new, but that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that your neighbourhood is about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half to the right from the road, and how long do you have to travel from the Pastrik Hotel in order to turn right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: From Hotel Pashtrik? You mean the road to Decan?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In order to take -- to turn right, you have to take the first turn right on this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The question was: How far from the centre of the town does one need to turn right? Is it immediately after the centre, or after 500 metres, or a kilometre, or a kilometre and a half, or 2 kilometres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: From Hotel Pashtrik you travel -- but you are asking me about two different roads. There are two roads, the one that goes to Decan and the one that goes to Kline. So I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the crossroads was our landmark, the road Klina-Decani. You said that one needed to turn right when moving from Orahovac towards Decani, that your neighbourhood was on the right-hand side. And you also told us that it was after the crossroads with the road leading to Klina. So I'm asking you, from this crossroads if you move on towards Decani, how long would you have to travel straight after this crossroads before you turn right to reach your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: If you are on the straight road from the hotel, from Hotel Pashtrik, there are the cross lights, the stop lights. You go to Decan in this way. Then you turn right. I would say it's about 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me, is the bus station near your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far from the bus station was your house located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: About 300 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And tell me, is the green market also somewhere in the vicinity of where your house used to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The question is: The green market, how far from your house is it? Is the green market situated in the same neighbourhood and relatively close to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: About 250 metres I would say. It's an approximation. It's not an accurate figure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we are talking approximately. But please tell me also, the old barracks in relation to the landmarks that we have mentioned, where is the old barracks located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The old barracks were located about one kilometre and a half from where my house was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us in which direction, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: In the direction of the centre of the town, where today the road to Prishtina is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me whether the Hadumit mosque and the library -- where are they located in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The Hadum mosque is very far from where I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell us, this elevated neighbourhood or the neighbourhood under construction that you mention in your statement, where was that located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please, because it's not clear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in several -- actually, in two places, you mentioned a neighbourhood that was under construction where you spent this evening, the night between the 2nd of April -- the 2nd of April in the morning, it was an elevated neighbourhood where you were. So what I would like to hear is if you could tell us where this neighbourhood was located in relation to your house or the bus station, if you could tell us where that neighbourhood is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I'm not clear about this question. I don't think I have said this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that it might be the right time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Djurdjic. We will now have a break which will enable the witness to have a drink and a rest, and we resume at 11.00. And Mr. Djurdjic will then continue with some questions. We adjourn now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning again, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic will continue now with his questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, if you could take your statement of April 1999 and turn to page 5, please, and that would be page 5 in the English version as well. Under item 18 in that paragraph. It says here: "The burning lasted in the neighbourhood until 4.00 a.m. and we could see it from a high point in the town in a neighbourhood that was being constructed." Have you found that passage in your statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Here you say that you were observing all that from a high point in a neighbourhood that was being constructed, and on page 6, please turn the page, in the paragraph which starts with "My family ..." you again say "this elevated neighbourhood where we hid the previous night." So what my question was: Where was this elevated neighbourhood located with reference to the bus station or your neighbourhood or the neighbourhood where your house stood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: From my neighbourhood it is about 50 or 60 metres away, whereas from the bus station about 300 to 350 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would that be a hill above your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. It is a plain about 50 or 60 metres away from my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would that place be behind your house or your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you, from the wall of your yard you reached the wall of your yard across that meadow, what is the distance from that point to the street, how far the street is from that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Which street?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To the main road, from that wall of your yard or compound, what is the distance from that point to the sidewalk of the main road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There are two main roads, in front of the house and behind the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if we go from that point towards your house, first we reach the road behind your house, at the back of your house; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And from the point where you were at that elevated neighbourhood to your lot, there was a distance of 50 metres, as you said; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: From my house to that house where we were sheltering and where we spent that night, there are about 50 metres to 60 metres in between.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is the distance from your house to the main road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Are you referring to the main road or to the house where we were sheltering?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean the main road. I don't want to name it. Your house was in such and such street at such and such number. What was the distance from your house where you used to live to the street whose number it bears?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Fifteen metres I would say, 15 to 20 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me, there was a yard around your house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, every house has a yard there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me whether there was a wall around your yard.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, in that neighbourhood every house has a walled-off yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, what was the distance from the wall of your yard to the neighbour's wall on your right-hand side when we're looking towards the street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The wall is between the two yards. As for the houses, the houses were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the number of metres.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- apart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that distance between the two houses.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know the exact distance, but the houses stand at a distance of 2 metres away from the wall between the two yards. So the total distance would be 5 to 6 metres maximum.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the same case be in the case of your left-hand neighbour and all the other houses in that neighbourhood along that street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes. The entire neighbourhood that was burned down, every house shared a wall with the house next to it -- every yard, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How tall were the yard walls, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: How tall it was? I would say about 1.80 metres to 2 metres tall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, when you testified in the Milutinovic et al. trial you said that you were 150 to 200 metres away, now you say 60, 70 metres tops.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I didn't measure the actual distance. I just gave an estimated distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the point you were, you could not see what was going in the main street from the intervening walls and houses; am I right in saying so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, you couldn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, sir, do you know where Vuk Karadzic Street used to be in March 1999 in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me what was your profession in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I was a tradesman for all my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I read somewhere that you're a car mechanic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you trade in car spare parts or any other trade back in 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I had a grocery shop, and we also sold tires.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us where your shop was located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I had a shop in my neighbourhood and another shop near the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were those shops open before your departure from Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, they were closed. We were staying at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you close those shops? When did you stop trading in those shops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: About two to three weeks before the NATO air-strikes began.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please tell me, until your departure from Djakovica had there been any air-strikes or bombardments of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us which part of Djakovica suffered bombing if it's known to you or if you went to those sites to see for yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I didn't go to those sites to see for myself, but they hit the barracks and Cabrat Hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, did you know Qamil Zherka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Qamil who? Can you repeat his last name, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Zherka.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And Sadik Nexhmedin Zherka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know -- Izet Hina [phoen] perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: He was a doctor. I never had any contact with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it known to you that on the 24th of March, from 2030 hours until 3.00 a.m. on the 25th of March, the old town of Djakovica was -- suffered bombing and that those persons were killed and that destruction was inflicted on both businesses and housing facilities in the old town of Djakovica. Is that known to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And what you heard about the Cabrat Hill and the old barracks, that was on the 25th of March at 8.00 p.m. or 2000 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact time because a long time has passed since. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you hear that on the 25th of March at 1955 in front of the Pastrik Hotel a policeman Danilovic, Nenad was attacked and severely wounded?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that because we were staying inside all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, did you hear that the Tabak bridge and Hadum mosque also bombed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear about that. I only know that people were saying that Cabrat and the military barracks were bombed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, sir, did you know Nimon and Bajram?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Bajram Nimonaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know Shaban Brahimaj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Where are these people from?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From Djakovica. This is why I'm asking you about them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From the beginning of 1999 until your departure from Djakovica, were you familiar with the activities of the KLA in Djakovica? Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, there were rumours about that, but personally I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I heard what you put to me, but personally I didn't see any of this activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what activities you heard and did not see for yourself. What did you hear about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I heard that the KLA had taken to the mountains. That's all basically I know about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, sir, please tell me, did you do your national conscription service?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did you leave, and where, the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I completed my military service in 1983/1984.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was your specialty and where, in which town did you serve?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I was a driver and I did my military service in Capljina and Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you returned home, were you a military reservist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. For a while we were but no longer than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me what kind of a uniform you had as a military reservist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The green army uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did all the reservists have green uniforms, military uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Those who were like me, reservists, they had the same uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as I can conclude, you are able to distinguish between police and military uniforms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement -- let me just ask you this before that. Since the beginning of the war, did you see people in uniforms moving around Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were police members and other uniforms. The entire town of Gjakova saw that, not only myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you distinguish between active soldiers and active-duty policemen and reserve military personnel and reserve policemen; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please have a look at your statement, page 4, and from the top it's the fifth paragraph beginning with the words: "Since the very first night of NATO bombing ..." And then the third sentence in this paragraph: "They were wearing bullet-proof vests and camouflage green uniforms ..." Is this part of your statement which you gave in April 1999 correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember what I gave then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, so as not to lose time, I have read this out to you. So the sentence says: "They were wearing bullet-proof vests and camouflage green uniforms ..." This is why the Prosecutor supplied you with the statement and this has been recorded in the transcript as something that's the best -- to the best of your knowledge. So this is why I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Where are you citing from? Which place do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, the usher gave you the statement. I saw that on the screen. I told you that this is page 4, and if we count the paragraphs from the top then it's the fifth paragraph. It begins with the words: "Since the very first night of NATO bombing ..." et cetera. So not that sentence, and not the next one, but the third one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't think I have seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And will you please tell me, the people in uniforms that you used to see, where did they work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I'm talking about the period before the war. They were in our neighbourhood. They were inhabitants of that neighbourhood for some 40, 50 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What I asked you was where did they work. Where were they employed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: They used to work in auto mechanic shops where cars are repaired.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would ask you to have a look at your statement which you were provided with and have a look at page 6 of this statement. And in the Albanian version it's page 5. And in the English version it's page 6. The paragraph beginning with the words: "I saw that my car had not been burned ..." Have you found this paragraph? It's the penultimate paragraph on that page, the page in Albanian. And in the last sentence in this paragraph you say: "He was also in the same green camouflage uniform worn by the Serbs described above." Witness, sir, is what I have just read out to you and what I hope you found in your statement, is this correct and is it true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I think that they did not properly understand you in the transcript and not all the places are correctly mentioned. You said that you set out from Djakovica on foot in the direction of the border crossing Cafa Prusit; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes Brekoc-Vogove-Zhub.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please just mention the place names slowly. The first place is Brekovo; am I right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, at the bridge, the road that goes to Brekoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you passed through Vogovo and then through a place called Zub?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever travel by car before this time from Djakovica to Cafa Prusit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, never in my life had I travelled to that area, but I have been -- I used to go to Brekoc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know what is the distance between Djakovica and Cafa Prusit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No, I don't know. Because as I said that was the only time I travelled to Qafa e Prushit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, sir, do you remember who of your neighbours was with you in the group that was going from Djakovica towards the border on the 2nd of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: All my neighbours, all the inhabitants of my neighbourhood went together. Every single family of my neighbourhood was part of the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the neighbours you remember were with you in the same group. Could you mention any of them by name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There are many. Should I mention all of them by name?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, who were the neighbours living closest to you that you can remember? I would ask you if you can remember to tell us their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will count all of them by names.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, how did it happen that you went and gave a statement to an investigator from the OTP in Tirana in April 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember, but when we crossed the border there were many cameramen from various countries and they took us to some camps there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember where it was that you gave your statement in April 1999?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: It was in Tirana, but I can't specify the particular place because it was the first and last time I was in Tirana so I don't remember the exact location where I gave that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how did you get to this place? Who took you there? Please don't mention the names if it might be someone from your neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember, really. It's such a long time ago. And as you might imagine, we were not in a very good condition. We suffered our traumas.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell me, who was present during this interview that you had with the investigator?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Present were people from the West. I don't know who they were, but they were from the West.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you first: How many persons were present while you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember what was the sex of the person or persons who were present, as you don't remember their number?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There were females and males. There were many people there. But I can't tell you exactly who they were and where that took place because, as I said, I was never before in Tirana so I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So we are through with this. You don't know who took you to the place where you gave your statement, but now we got to this place where you gave the statement. So you were giving the statement. My first question was if you knew how many persons were present while you were giving the statement, and now it's not really clear to me because you mention a number of people. Was there a number of people present in the room while you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The place resembled an embassy or something like that. There were many employees there who would enter and leave the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would like to ask you to focus and listen very carefully to my questions so that you can provide an answer, so that we use this time efficiently. I'm not asking you about how many people were in the building. But in the room where you were giving your statement were there many more people giving their statements or just you giving your statement in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Maybe three or four persons. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Those three persons giving statements, were they also from your neighbourhood, from your part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. One of them spoke English, the other knew Italian, and the third I don't know which language he spoke. They were not from my town or from my neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned, as far as I can conclude, the persons you mentioned just now are the people who spoke to you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which languages do you speak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Do you mean me?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I speak my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How did you communicate with those persons who were in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: There was an interpreter as well who spoke Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, were you shown statements of other people or any documents while you were talking to those people in that room?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I mean the people who talked to you, did they read statements given by other people or did they show you or read out from documents? Did they have to refresh your memory? That's what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: No. Those who gave statements before me, they gave the statements individually, in separate rooms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you gave your statement on the 23rd of April, 1999. Before starting giving your statement, did you speak to anybody who provided their statement before you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember, really. A long time has passed since then. I did meet people from my neighbourhood while in Tirana. We did discuss what happened to us. But long time has passed since, and I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember how many days it took you to give your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think it was short. It didn't last long.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this a verbal conversation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, it was a verbal conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was a written statement produced on that occasion while you were giving your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember. Honestly, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you sign a statement in writing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I really don't remember right now. There were ups and downs. We were traumatised, so I really don't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show the B/C/S version of the written statement to the witness, please -- I apologise, not the B/C/S but the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you've seen the witness statement shown to you by the usher. Does your signature appear to be on any part of that statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did this refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when the signing of this statement took place, and do you know what you signed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I don't remember. This is my signature, but I don't remember when I signed this statement. A long time has passed since.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But do you remember where you were while you were signing this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: As I said, I was in Tirana.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, we know that you were in Tirana, but which location in Tirana was this statement produced while you signed it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: As I said, that was the first time I ever visited Tirana, and I'm not familiar with the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this in the same building in which you gave your statement or at some other place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: I think it was in the same building in which we had a conversation, but I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me, do you understand this statement which you signed? Can you read it? Do you understand anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, please turn to page 2 which bears the signature. My question is: Can you read this, can you understand what you're reading, and the contents of the witness statement, I mean the signed witness statement before you? Do you understand me? Can you read and understand what is written on page 2 of the statement that you signed? This is my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: The statement which is signed is in English and I don't understand English. I understand the beginning. On the 1st of April in 1999, I understand this part in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And further, do you understand any other parts of the statement which do not contain time references, dates, numbers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, please continue reading the witness statement beyond the first five words. And do you understand what is written here in English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS K74
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... English. It's in English. I don't read English. If you want me to clarify something, ask me and I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
